arithmetic_input: Original weights w_(p^k)=log(p)*p^(-k/2) give the complete Poisson symbol P_p(theta)=1+2*sum_(k>=1) p^(-k/2)*cos(k*theta).
candidate_inference: With the original archimedean and pole terms, prime locations, positive prime-power weights and first-window nonnegativity retained, the prime-chain operator bounds m_p I <= C_p <= M_p I for every prime exclude a nonzero nullvector at that window. Here m_p=(1-p^(-1/2))/(1+p^(-1/2)), M_p=1/m_p, and C_p uses the complete chain with constant Fourier coefficient one.
scope_of_candidate: This tests sufficiency of the bounds derived from Euler coefficients. It does not test a theorem that retains the exact geometric coefficient identities as an additional premise. Losing that distinction would overstate the control.

controls_before_proof.Davenport_Heilbronn: Use controls/davenport_heilbronn.py screen interface, record not-applicable: it does not preserve the stipulated original conductor, gamma/poles or this original real prime-chain coefficient family.

quantifiers_and_budget: Candidate bounds for all primes, all Fourier frequencies and all finite windows. One explicit perturbation, 50/80-digit diagnostic screen, then elementary exact bounds only if the hypothesis match survives. No scan for a first-zero window or new certificate.
success_consequence: A distinguishing independent inequality would still need its own full proposal and proof; positive samples alone cannot admit API.
failure_consequence: If the exact original bounds survive the NS57 first-zero control, stop the positivity-only inference. Do not close original API, exact Euler recursions or bounded-floor methods.
